summary: Scoped Phase 1 Universe rules assessment: current and legacy submissions, drafts, revision links, locks, idempotency, membership/task status and private Universe audit events are API-only. Owner navigation preferences have bounded typed create/update validation. The local emulator suites pass 131 tests; the service/API suite passes 65 and all three real-client mission flows pass. No unresolved finding remains in this explicitly limited rules scope. This is not a whole-application security certification or a deployed-system assessment.

evidence.api: 65/65, 5 files, local Auth 9399 and Firestore 8288, same demo project
evidence.realClientFlow: 3 routes + parent scenario pass; save/replay/concurrent submit/return/revise/review and no grants

checks.evidence: Both universe-v1 owning matches apply the same field/type/bounds checks to create and update. Invalid nested/oversized/non-string ID values, delimiter tricks, 51 entries and cross-owner writes are denied; all 50 maximum-length valid IDs succeed.

Client-writable profile fields cannot grant Universe organization/class authority. API verifies current Auth claims/protected membership and current org/rosters, including stale-token replay; raw client record reads/writes are denied.

Actual API, using privileged server transactions, provides permitted drafts/history/reviews. Client direct access is unnecessary; scoped owner/coach paths and legacy read-only history remain served by API.

Navigation list is at most 50 ASCII IDs of 1–64 characters (3,200 ID characters plus separators), preference maps use a bounded allowlist. Family lock has scalar counters; immutable per-attempt revision links avoid growing arrays/maps. Server enforces 64 KiB requests/records and reviewed-record size.
Explicit list element types plus bounded joined-ID shape; malformed nested maps/booleans/null and excessive lengths fail closed. Shared validation bounds all submitted evidence and authority fields.
Preference rules require the existing owner identity as well as schema allowlists; cross-owner writes fail. Universe records/private audit events have no client role bypass.
Restrictions are inside owning preference rules. Default recursive rule denies access. Flat legacy audit reader does not match nested Universe audit events; get/list/write denials are tested.

limits: Only the listed Universe paths and their relevant profile boundary are assessed. Other application collections and legacy flat audit readers are outside this score.

No production rules deployment or production data inspection occurred. Existing real pilot account provisioning, any legacy flat Universe audit data and applicable rollout operations require their own preflight before activation.
Student-device, touch and assistive-technology validation is the next round requested by Mani.
